d: Explains the process of customizing the loading screen when users are connecting to your game.
h:
Roblox displays a default loading screen when users are connecting to a game, but you can personalize your game with a custom loading screen that contains static or animated content.

This article covers the loading screens that display when a user initially joins a game. To customize loading screens that display when a user teleports between places, see Teleport between places.

Implementation

To display a custom loading screen, you can either design a ScreenGui instance directly within a LocalScript, or you can reference a ScreenGui object in your place hierarchy. Both options utilize ReplicatedFirst, as this service that replicates instances to clients before anything else is replicated. This ensures that your loading screen is the first thing users see when they enter your game.

From script

To design and display a custom loading screen entirely from a LocalScript:

  1. In ReplicatedFirst, create a LocalScript.
  2. Paste in the following code sample to create and customize a ScreenGui object. You can modify the following code with your own values to create your design.

Script-Created Loading Screen

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedFirst = game:GetService("ReplicatedFirst")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local loadingScreen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
loadingScreen.IgnoreGuiInset = true
loadingScreen.Parent = playerGui

-- Replace ScreenGui values with your own
local textLabel = Instance.new("TextLabel")
textLabel.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
textLabel.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(0, 20, 40)
textLabel.Font = Enum.Font.DenkOne
textLabel.TextColor3 = Color3.new(0.8, 0.8, 0.8)
textLabel.Text = "Loading"
textLabel.TextSize = 32
textLabel.Parent = loadingScreen

-- Remove the default loading screen
ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()

task.wait(5)  -- Force custom loading screen to appear for a minimum time

if not game:IsLoaded() then
    game.Loaded:Wait()
end

loadingScreen:Destroy()

From existing GUI

Instead of creating a loading screen ScreenGui entirely through a LocalScript, you can also reference an existing ScreenGui in your place hierarchy. Ensure that your game includes the referenced ScreenGui within ReplicatedFirst and that the ScreenGui includes UI elements like TextLabels and ImageLabels.

To demonstrate this process, the following LocalScript references a ScreenGui named LoadingScreen within ReplicatedFirst, then it removes the default loading screen so the only loading screen a player can see is your own custom loading screen.

Remember that you can design your loading screen ScreenGui within the StarterGui container to preview it, then move it to ReplicatedFirst once you're satisfied with the result.

Reference Existing Loading Screen

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedFirst = game:GetService("ReplicatedFirst")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local loadingScreen = ReplicatedFirst:FindFirstChild("LoadingScreen")
if loadingScreen then
    loadingScreen.IgnoreGuiInset = true
    loadingScreen.Parent = playerGui

    -- Remove the default loading screen
    ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()

    task.wait(5)  -- Force screen to appear for a minimum number of seconds

    if not game:IsLoaded() then
        game.Loaded:Wait()
    end

    loadingScreen:Destroy()
end

Add animations

In addition to static custom loading screens, you can add animations to enhance the loading screen and indicate loading progress. The easiest way to do this is to create a UI element, such as a TextLabel or ImageLabel, then to animate it using TweenService. For example, the following code sample creates a new ScreenGui with a child ImageLabel, removes the default loading screen, then TweenService fades in and rotates the central elements until the game loads.

Script-Created Loading Screen (Animated)

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedFirst = game:GetService("ReplicatedFirst")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local loadingScreen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
loadingScreen.IgnoreGuiInset = true
loadingScreen.Parent = playerGui

local textLabel = Instance.new("TextLabel")
textLabel.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
textLabel.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(0, 20, 40)
textLabel.Font = Enum.Font.DenkOne
textLabel.TextColor3 = Color3.new(0.8, 0.8, 0.8)
textLabel.Text = "Loading"
textLabel.TextSize = 32
textLabel.TextTransparency = 1
textLabel.Parent = loadingScreen

local loadingRing = Instance.new("ImageLabel")
loadingRing.Size = UDim2.new(0, 256, 0, 256)
loadingRing.BackgroundTransparency = 1
loadingRing.Image = "rbxassetid://4965945816"
loadingRing.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
loadingRing.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
loadingRing.ImageTransparency = 1
loadingRing.Parent = loadingScreen

-- Remove the default loading screen
ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()

-- Initiate and start fade-in tweens
local fadeTweenInfo = TweenInfo.new(1, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out, 0, false, 2)
local fadeTween1 = TweenService:Create(textLabel, fadeTweenInfo, {TextTransparency = 0})
local fadeTween2 = TweenService:Create(loadingRing, fadeTweenInfo, {ImageTransparency = 0})
fadeTween1:Play()
fadeTween2:Play()

-- Initiate and start rotation tween
local tweenInfo = TweenInfo.new(4, Enum.EasingStyle.Linear, Enum.EasingDirection.In, -1)
local tween = TweenService:Create(loadingRing, tweenInfo, {Rotation = 360})
tween:Play()

task.wait(5)  -- Force screen to appear for a minimum number of seconds

if not game:IsLoaded() then
    game.Loaded:Wait()
end

loadingScreen:Destroy()

kid.simple: When someone joins your game, Roblox shows a plain loading screen while things download. You can swap it for your own screen with your game's name, colors, or a spinning logo. This page shows how to build one with a LocalScript in `ReplicatedFirst`, how to remove the default one, and how to animate yours with `TweenService`. A good loading screen makes your game feel polished from the very first second.
kid.analogy: It is like the curtain in a theater. While the stage crew sets up behind it, the audience looks at a nice curtain with the show's name on it instead of a messy stage.
keyPoints: Put a LocalScript in `ReplicatedFirst`. Things in `ReplicatedFirst` reach the player's device before anything else, so your screen shows up first.
You can build the `ScreenGui` in code, or design it ahead of time and keep it in `ReplicatedFirst`.
Parent your screen to the player's `PlayerGui` and set `IgnoreGuiInset = true` so it covers the whole screen, including the top bar area.
Call `ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()` so only your screen shows.
Wait until `game:IsLoaded()` is true, or wait for `game.Loaded`, then destroy your screen.
Add a `task.wait()` if you want your screen to stay up for a minimum time, like 5 seconds.
Use `TweenService` to fade in text or spin an image to show that loading is happening.
You can design the screen in `StarterGui` to preview it, then move it to `ReplicatedFirst` when done.
This page is about joining. Teleport loading screens are set up differently, with `SetTeleportGui()`.

terms.ReplicatedFirst: A special container whose contents get copied to the player's device before anything else in the game.
terms.replicate: Copy from the server to a player's device so it exists there too.
terms.ScreenGui: The container that holds 2D things drawn on the screen, like labels and images.
terms.PlayerGui: The folder inside each player that holds the screens they can currently see.
terms.IgnoreGuiInset: When `true`, the screen also covers the strip at the top where Roblox's buttons are, so there is no gap.
terms.UDim2: A size or position for 2D UI. `UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)` means 100% of the width and 100% of the height, plus 0 extra pixels each.
terms.tween: A smooth change from one value to another over time, like fading transparency from `1` (invisible) to `0` (fully visible) in 1 second.
terms.TweenInfo: Settings for a tween: how long it takes, its easing style, and how many times it repeats. A repeat count of `-1` means repeat forever.
terms.Transparency: How see-through something is. `0` is solid and `1` is fully invisible.
terms.game.Loaded: An event that fires once everything in the game has finished loading on the player's device.

example.title: A simple custom loading screen
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedFirst = game:GetService("ReplicatedFirst")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

-- Make a screen that covers everything
local loadingScreen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
loadingScreen.IgnoreGuiInset = true
loadingScreen.Parent = playerGui

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0) -- full width and height
label.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(0, 20, 40)
label.TextColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
label.Text = "Loading my game..."
label.TextSize = 32
label.Parent = loadingScreen

-- Hide Roblox's default loading screen
ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()

task.wait(3) -- show our screen for at least 3 seconds

if not game:IsLoaded() then
	game.Loaded:Wait() -- wait until everything has loaded
end

loadingScreen:Destroy()
explain: The script runs on the player's device very early because it lives in `ReplicatedFirst`.
It makes a `ScreenGui` and a full-screen `TextLabel` with dark blue background and white text.
`RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()` hides the Roblox one, so only yours is visible.
It waits at least 3 seconds, then waits for the game to finish loading if it has not yet.
Finally, `Destroy()` removes the loading screen and the player sees the game.

watchOut: Putting the LocalScript somewhere other than `ReplicatedFirst`. It will run too late and players will see the default screen first.
Forgetting to destroy the loading screen. Players will be stuck staring at it forever.
Leaving out `IgnoreGuiInset = true`, which leaves a gap at the top of your screen.
Using a regular Script instead of a LocalScript. Loading screens run on the player's device.
